text:
Alex (PM): quick thread — drafting SLOs for next release. proposal: tiered latency SLOs + explicit error-budget burn actions + graceful degrade to distilled models. need acceptance criteria and edge cases.

Sam (SRE): please put concrete numbers. also circuit-breaker thresholds and what 'degrade' actually means operationally.

Jordan (Eng Runtime): runtime notes: we can route by model variant and token-length bucket. fallback path to `gpt-embed-fast` / `chat-distill-v1` is trivial to wire but there are quality regressions to accept.

Maya (Product): enterprise asks: Customer X is asking for 250ms p95 on chat for Dedicated. is that in-scope or a separate SLA negotiation?

Liam (ML Infra): embeddings fine for single calls, bulk jobs cause high tail. suggest separate SLO for bulk/batch endpoints (per-request vs per-job).

Priya (CS): FYI Customer X will expect SLA credit language if p99 breaches their committed window. need to sync legal.

Alex (PM): concrete proposal below — feedback welcome.
- Scope: chat/generate endpoints, embeddings (single), embeddings-bulk (batch).
- Tiers: free / paid-hosted / dedicated.
- Targets (p95 / p99):
  - chat: free 600ms / 2.5s, paid 300ms / 1.2s, dedicated 200ms / 600ms
  - generate (non-chat): free 400ms / 1.8s, paid 220ms / 900ms, dedicated 150ms / 500ms
  - embeddings (single): free 200ms / 800ms, paid 120ms / 400ms, dedicated 80ms / 250ms
  - embeddings-bulk: throughput SLO: 95% of jobs finish within expected time-slots (depends on batch size); detailed formula in PRD.
- Error budget policy: if burn_rate > 4 for 30m -> pause rollouts + notify; if burn_rate > 8 for 15m -> rollback and page @Oncall.

Jordan (Eng Runtime): can we define 'burn_rate' metric name? I suggest `error_budget_burn_rate{route,model_variant}` and include it in dashboards. Also runtime needs a safe fast-fail for very long requests (hard timeout).

Sam (SRE): add circuit-breaker rules: if request error rate > 1% for 5m AND p99 > threshold -> open circuit for that model_variant for 10m and route traffic to fallback. example alert: 
```
alert: HighErrorBudgetBurn
expr: error_budget_burn_rate > 4
for: 30m
labels: {severity: "warning"}
---
expr: error_budget_burn_rate > 8
for: 15m
labels: {severity: "critical"}
```
On critical -> page.

Maya (Product): acceptance criteria for this launch:
- Synthetic bench must show p95 within 10% of target for all tiers under representative load.
- No quality regression > 2 pts on evals when using fallback models.
- Canary rollout policy in place (see Jordan).

Jordan (Eng Runtime): proposed canary flow: 5% traffic 6h, if OK -> 25% 24h, if OK -> 100% 72h. immediate rollback if p99 breaches during canary or burn_rate spikes.

Liam (ML Infra): edge-case: very long prompts (>> typical tokens) create KV cache pressure and unpredictably high latency. mitigation: token-length routing + soft reject suggestion to user with `truncation_policy=long_prompt_suggest` or route to dedicated capacity only. add explicit acceptance test for 10k-token spike.

Alex (PM): runbook items to include in PRD: how to change routing policy, who toggles 'force-fallback' flag, escalation matrix, SLA credit owner, steps to pause rollouts. I'll draft. Assigning: Jordan -> runtime knobs, Sam -> alert rules and burn definitions, Maya -> acceptance criteria and customer-facing SLA language, Liam -> fallback model quality eval and token-routing spec, Priya -> customer sign-off process and legal.

Priya (CS): I'll start customer X sync. ask: can we offer a dedicated latency SLA addendum for them as a paid attachment?

Sam (SRE): also add cost impact note: automatic fallback to distill reduces infra cost but may increase eval hits for quality monitoring. need cost guardrail.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary rollout 1729034567 -> 5% traffic to `chat-distill-v1` for validation :rocket: 

Oncall Bot: reminder — new alert rules created in staging. watch for flapping during first 2h.

Alex (PM): thanks everyone — I'll put this into the PRD draft and ping people for quick reviews. goal: finalize SLO text + runbook by EOD Friday. :calendar:
